title: A dispatch table
description:
Route requests to handlers by their major function, as `DriverObject->MajorFunction` does.

```
IRP_MJ_CREATE  -> createClose: STATUS_SUCCESS
IRP_MJ_READ    -> read: STATUS_SUCCESS, 12 bytes
IRP_MJ_WRITE   -> not handled: STATUS_INVALID_DEVICE_REQUEST
every request completed exactly once
```
hints: Fill the whole table with the default first, then set the ones you handle (lesson 2.02).
Completing an IRP twice is a classic driver bug that crashes the system; the flag here catches it.
requirements: An array of 28 handler pointers, all set to a default that fails the request.
`complete(irp, status, information)` records the result and refuses to complete twice.
Handlers return the status they completed with.
stretch: Add `IRP_MJ_CLEANUP` and explain how it differs from close.
